differences.title: 1. CORE ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: Actix-web leverages the actor model for concurrent message passing, enabling highly scalable and fault-tolerant applications through isolated, independent actors.
differences.rightDesc: Axum is built on the Tower service abstraction, composing asynchronous request handlers into robust middleware chains for flexible request processing.

differences.title: 2. ASYNCHRONOUS RUNTIME
differences.leftDesc: Actix-web uses its own actor-based runtime, optimized for its actor model, providing efficient task scheduling and non-blocking I/O operations.
differences.rightDesc: Axum is tightly integrated with Tokio, Rust's de facto async runtime, offering a mature ecosystem for I/O, scheduling, and synchronization primitives.

differences.title: 3. DEPENDENCY INJECTION
differences.leftDesc: State is managed and shared via actor context and messages, allowing controlled access to application-wide data and resources.
differences.rightDesc: Axum utilizes `State` extensions to pass shared application state down the middleware chain, offering a simpler, direct approach.

differences.title: 4. MIDDLEWARE COMPOSITION
differences.leftDesc: Actix-web uses attribute macros on handlers and application objects to define middleware behavior, offering concise configuration.
differences.rightDesc: Axum composes middleware by chaining `Tower` services, providing a highly flexible and composable way to add cross-cutting concerns.

differences.title: 5. ROUTING FLEXIBILITY
differences.leftDesc: Actix-web provides robust routing based on URL paths and HTTP methods, with flexible extraction of route parameters.
differences.rightDesc: Axum offers similar powerful routing capabilities, allowing intricate path definitions and easy parameter extraction, integrated with its service architecture.

differences.title: 6. ERROR HANDLING
differences.leftDesc: Actix-web handles errors by returning `Result` types from handlers, which are then converted into appropriate HTTP responses.
differences.rightDesc: Axum leverages `Tower::Layer` and `Tower::Service` error handling, enabling standardized and consistent error propagation through middleware.

differences.title: 7. COMMUNITY & ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Actix-web has a mature ecosystem with extensive features and a long history in Rust web development, offering stability.
differences.rightDesc: Axum is rapidly gaining popularity, backed by Tokio, and benefits from the modern Rust async ecosystem and Tower's composability.
